intended_object: For a continuous map g : X → Y, the canonical natural isomorphism between the underlying sheaf of sets of the inverse-image sheaf of rings g⁻¹A and the inverse image of the underlying sheaf of sets of A. This is the standard fact that taking the inverse image of a sheaf of commutative rings commutes with forgetting to sheaves of sets. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is the inverse (`.symm`) of `canonicalComparisonIso`. That isomorphism is assembled with `NatIso.ofComponents` from `canonicalComponent g A`, and `canonicalComponent_naturality` supplies naturality. `canonicalComponent g A` is the adjunction mate, for the pullback ⊣ pushforward adjunction of Type-valued sheaves, of the underlying map of sets of the unit A → g_* g⁻¹ A of the ring-valued adjunction. That is exactly the canonical comparison map g⁻¹(forget A) → forget(g⁻¹A). The file proves it is an isomorphism for every A (`canonicalComponent_isIso`), so the components are the right ones.

The type of the declaration, `pullback CommRingCat g ⋙ underlyingSheaf X ≅ underlyingSheaf Y ⋙ pullback (Type v) g`, goes from the forgotten ring pullback to the pullback of the forgotten sheaf, as the docstring says. Its inverse component is the canonical mate (`inverseComparisonIso_inv_app`).

On generality: the same comparison exists for any concrete category whose forgetful functor is compatible with sheafification, and over general sites. The library itself has a parallel AbelianForget version. However, Mathlib has no general version of this isomorphism; grepping for combinations of pullback and `sheafCompose` found nothing. The ring-sheaf case on topological spaces is a standard statement in its own right, so I do not count this as too narrow.

This declaration is only the reversed direction of `canonicalComparisonIso`, but it still names the canonical isomorphism correctly.
